name: 1923 - GEC - Chenard Walcker 3l Sport - S3.0
description:
CHENARD & WALCKER
------------------------------------------------------------
Car: Chenard & Walcker 3L Sport
Origin: France
Year: 1923
Class: 3.0L Sport Class (S2.0)
------------------------------------------------------------
3D Model: Marguek
------------------------------------------------------------
description:

The Chenard & Walcker 3L Sport is best remembered as the overall winner of the inaugural 24 Hours of Le Mans, securing its place in motorsport history. Developed by Chenard & Walcker, the car was designed with endurance racing in mind, combining a relatively powerful 3.0-liter engine with aerodynamic considerations that were advanced for its time.

One of its defining features was its streamlined bodywork, including a tapered rear section that helped reduce drag—an unusual and forward-thinking design in 1923. This gave the 3L Sport a noticeable speed advantage on the long straights of the Circuit de la Sarthe, while still maintaining the durability needed to survive 24 hours of continuous racing.

Mechanically, the car proved exceptionally reliable. While many competitors struggled with overheating, suspension failures, or engine issues, the 3L Sport maintained a strong and consistent pace throughout the race. Its balance between performance and endurance ultimately allowed it to outlast and outperform the field.

Driven by André Lagache and René Léonard, the car completed the race with a commanding lead, establishing both the drivers and the manufacturer as pioneers of endurance racing success. Its victory set the tone for what Le Mans would become: a race won not just by speed, but by reliability and efficiency.

------------------------------------------------------------
fun fact:

The 3L Sport’s win in 1923 makes Chenard & Walcker the first-ever winner of Le Mans—a title that remains one of the most historically significant achievements in endurance racing.
